title: 🤖 Editor crashes with STATUS_ILLEGAL_INSTRUCTION in Thread::wait_to_finish during script documentation regeneration
body:
> [!INFO]
> *AI disclosure*: This contribution was authored by an autonomous AI agent, on behalf of a user, to report a crash found in their project's CI.
>
> I found this crash myself, in my own project's CI, where I have been tracking it as saworbit/didi#285 across six occurrences. The reproduction environment and the artifacts are mine and the investigation ran under my direction. I then used an AI agent to symbolize the stack, trace it back through the engine source, and write it up.

### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: 4.7.2.stable and 4.5.1.stable.
- Not bisected.

### System information

Windows Server 2022 (GitHub Actions windows-latest) - Godot v4.7.2.stable.official [ed1daf0bf] - D3D12 12_0 (Forward+) - Microsoft Basic Render Driver

### Issue description

The editor dies with exit code `0xC000001D` (illegal instruction) and prints nothing.

The faulting instruction is a `ud2` inside `Thread::wait_to_finish()`, on the thread running `EditorHelp::_finish_regen_script_doc_thread()`:

```
thread 5496, main thread is 5892
  #00 Godot_v4.7.2-stable_win64.exe+0x066744b6   ud2
  #01 Godot_v4.7.2-stable_win64.exe+0x017a6266   EditorHelp::_finish_regen_script_doc_thread
  #02 Godot_v4.7.2-stable_win64.exe+0x03928abd   Thread::callback
  #03 Godot_v4.7.2-stable_win64.exe+0x04cf4b1a   std::thread trampoline
  #04 msvcrt.dll / KERNEL32.DLL / ntdll.dll
```

Both `ERR_FAIL` guards in `wait_to_finish()` pass. The trap is `std::thread::join()`'s own preconditions, inlined after them. Exceptions are disabled, so libstdc++'s throw folds to `__builtin_trap()`, which is why there is no message:

```
core/os/thread.cpp:84   ERR_FAIL_COND_MSG(id == UNASSIGNED_ID, ...)      passes
core/os/thread.cpp:85   ERR_FAIL_COND_MSG(id == get_caller_id(), ...)    passes
core/os/thread.cpp:86   thread.join()
                        -> !joinable()                  -> ud2
                        -> get_id() == this_thread::get_id() -> ud2
```

So `join()` ran on a `Thread` whose `std::thread` was already consumed or not yet constructed, while `id` still said it was started.

That looks reachable because `Thread` has no lock: `id` and `thread` (`core/os/thread.h:108`, `:113`) are plain members, `start()` sets `id` before constructing `thread`, and `wait_to_finish()` clears `thread` before `id`. `EditorHelp` then joins the same two static threads from several places without serialising:

- `get_doc_data()` -> `_wait_for_thread()` — main thread (`editor/doc/editor_help.cpp:2966`)
- `regenerate_script_doc_cache()` -> `_wait_for_thread(worker_thread)`, `_wait_for_thread(loader_thread)` — main thread (`:3176`)
- `_finish_regen_script_doc_thread()` -> `loader_thread.wait_to_finish()` — worker thread (`:3183`)

`_wait_for_thread()` checks `is_started()` and then calls `wait_to_finish()` as two steps, so the answer can change in between.

I cannot prove the exact interleaving from one dump.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open a project with GDScript files in the editor.
2. Trigger script documentation regeneration, which runs on `sources_changed` after a filesystem scan that saw script changes.
3. While that is running, make the main thread enter `EditorHelp`, for example by opening a scene so the inspector resolves class documentation.

In my case an external tool drives the editor over IPC and does this repeatedly. It hits roughly 1 run in 6 to 1 in 11. The rate rose sharply when I changed that tool to open its first scene immediately after the filesystem scan settles, which is exactly when `regenerate_script_doc_cache()` starts.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

N/A. This is a race between the editor's own documentation threads and its main thread, not project content. I could not reduce it to a project and click path that reproduces reliably.

I have a 222 KB minidump with all 32 thread stacks, and the full crash report, if either is useful. Happy to run an instrumented build.
